user_scenario:
You are Desmond Okoro, 37, an order picker at the Northgate Fulfillment Partners distribution center outside Columbus. It is Saturday morning; you are calling Paystride between waves on the warehouse floor, speaking in short, practical sentences and a bit impatient because you are on the clock. Your car payment comes out of your Chase checking account today and the account is nearly empty, so you want the biggest instant transfer of your earned pay that Paystride will give you, pushed right now to your Chase debit card, the one you have used with Paystride before. You say that up front: as much as you can get, instantly, to your Chase debit card, today. You do not want it on your Paystride card for this, because the car payment pulls from Chase; if the agent suggests the card, you say no, it has to be the Chase debit card. You have no figure in mind and you will take whatever the maximum is. If the agent asks why money is tight, you say you were out sick most of the last pay period and nothing from your last paycheck showed up on your card; you do not know the details of what was taken out of it.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Desmond Okoro, and your mobile number, 7135550158. If they need another detail, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 4632. Only if they still ask do you give your date of birth, 1988-11-02, your ZIP code, 43219, or your email, desmond.okoro@quickpost.net. If asked for your employee number, it is 40263. If asked whether you already took any early pay today, you say yes, you moved some onto your Paystride card first thing this morning for groceries, and you leave the amount to the agent to look up. If asked whether you work anywhere else that uses Paystride, you say no. If asked whether you have a Paystride payroll loan, you say no. If asked about the debit card, you say a push to it failed once back in June because the card had been reissued, and it has worked since.

You are fine with the agent doing whatever they need to do on their side. The transfer is your call, so when the agent tells you how much you can get and what the instant transfer will cost, you say that is fine, and when the agent hands the transfer to you to confirm, you confirm it yourself using exactly the plan reference, amount and sequence number the agent gives you. If the confirmation shows a reference number and the agent asks for it, you read it back. If the amount is lower than you hoped, you grumble that it is less than you thought but say to go ahead; you never offer a different number. When the agent tells you the transfer is all set, you say thanks, you have to get back to work, and hang up.
